Definition: from G575 and the base of G2949; to breed forth, i.e. (by transference) to generate (figuratively):--beget, produce.
BiblicalUsage: Twice in James, and the two verses are a birth and a birth. Lust, when it hath conceived, bringeth forth sin, and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death in James 1:15 — but of His own will God begat us with the word of truth in James 1:18, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of His creatures.
TheologicalSignificance: The same word bears two children, and I must choose which birth I belong to: sin's, which ends in death, or God's, which begins in truth.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
